issue.body:
fix(forms): ensure to emit status change events on subsequent value-update / validations

RCA:

During initialization of FormControl, `emitEvent` is getting passed as `false` to `updateValueAndValidity` function, in turn the same value got passed to the `_runAsyncValidator` function. (sets status = 'PENDING') and asyncValidator will be invoked.
When we set the `FormControl` to the `FormGroup` via `FormGroup.setcontrol`, internally it is calling `updateValueAndValidity` (on FormGroup) function with `emitEvent` as undefined, it causes status change event to be emitted on `FormGroup` instance. (causes 'PENDING' status change event)
When the asyncValidator (of FormControl) got resolved, `setErrors` function is getting invoked by passing the lexical scoped variable `emitEvent` (false in this case).
As emitEvent value is `false`, susbsequent status change events are not getting notified !!

If I understand correctly, status-change-events needs to be notified on value update / validations.

Please correct me, If I am wrong.

Issue: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/20424

body:
What happens when you listen to the control itself like so:

```
myForm.get('myControl').statusChanges
  .subscribe(status => console.log(status));

```
?

This issue still exists for me in ng v. 6.0.5. I registered myself to the statusChanges event and it is not fired for the result. I only get the notification for the transition to pending.

In essence this makes it currently quiet hard to use the async validator properly. Are there already some straight forward workarounds?

I am also experiencing this problem. 
Workarounds / fix due please?
Are you sure your async validator is completing? I had similar behaviour in TestBed u till I added  `take(1)` to my `AsyncValidatorFn`.
@Endran @varghesep it feels like you did not look at the [demo](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-qmdbkx). Your suggestions do not fit in any way.
Yeah, I was a bit to hasty. Nevermind.

@dzonatan I'm sorry for my previous comment. Removing ```changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush``` did not help. But I'm very surprised to note that the same code works on a parent (container) reactive form, but the same code in a child (contained) does not work. In the parent form, the status changes from PENDING to VALID or INVALID, but for the child, it is stuck on PENDING. I can't figure this out because the template and code are exactly the name between the forms.

The angular documentation on [this page](https://angular.io/guide/form-validation) says:

> The observable returned must be finite, meaning it must complete at some point. To convert an infinite observable into a finite one, pipe the observable through a filtering operator such as first, last, take, or takeUntil.

I even tried what they suggested, but that did not help.
What about this issue? We still have trouble with this behavior. Is a fix anywhere near?
